# `sesam config reset` rewrites sesam.yml to describe the audit log again,
# throwing away whatever the file declared on top of it. It is the opposite of
# `sesam config apply` and never touches the log.

exec git init
exec git config user.email test@sesam.dev
exec git config user.name 'Sesam Test'

exec sesam init --user admin
exec sesam tell --user bob --recipient $BOB_PUBKEY --group dev
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'init sesam'

# Nothing to do when the two already agree.
exec sesam config reset
stdout 'nothing to reset'

# Hand edits are discarded, and the diff is empty afterwards.
cp edited.yml sesam.yml
envsubst sesam.yml
exec sesam config diff
stdout '\+  - name: carol'

# --dry-run reports the same outcome and writes nothing.
exec sesam config reset --dry-run
stdout '\+ user carol \(groups: dev'
stdout 'would discard 2 declared changes'
stdout 'was not touched'
exec sesam config diff
stdout '\+  - name: carol'

exec sesam config reset
stdout '\+ user carol \(groups: dev'
stdout '~ secret README.md access: admin -> dev'
stdout 'discarded 2 declared changes'
exec sesam config diff
stdout 'in sync'

# The audit log is untouched by all of this.
exec sesam user list
stdout 'bob'
! stdout 'carol'
exec sesam verify

# A config too broken to read is rewritten from the audit log instead. Here the
# file is not YAML at all.
cp broken.yml sesam.yml
exec sesam config reset --dry-run
stdout 'cannot be reused'
stdout 'would be lost'
grep 'valid yaml at all' sesam.yml

exec sesam config reset
stdout 'cannot be reused'
stdout 'comments and descriptions are gone'

# What it wrote describes the log exactly, so apply has nothing to do.
exec sesam config diff
stdout 'in sync'
exec sesam apply
stdout 'nothing to apply'
exec sesam verify

# Even a deleted sesam.yml is recoverable.
rm sesam.yml
exec sesam config reset
stdout 'cannot be reused'
exists sesam.yml
exec sesam config diff
stdout 'in sync'

# The rewritten file has every user and secret the log knows.
grep 'name: admin' sesam.yml
grep 'name: bob' sesam.yml
grep 'README.md' sesam.yml

-- edited.yml --
users:
  - name: admin
    key:
      - $ADMIN_PUBKEY
  - name: bob
    key:
      - $BOB_PUBKEY
  - name: carol
    key:
      - $CAROL_PUBKEY

groups:
  admin:
    - admin
  dev:
    - bob
    - carol

secrets:
  - path: README.md
    access:
      - dev

-- broken.yml --
this is: [not
  valid yaml at all
